groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: A person may not submit a bid or work as a contractor until that person has been issued a certificate of registration as a contractor by the department.

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development, unless the context indicates otherwise

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development, unless the context indicates otherwise

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.quote: "commissioner," unless the text reads otherwise, means the commissioner of the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.
Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.
Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.
Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.
The comparable education FLOOR as a normalized rung. Populate whenever licensure is gated on a degree; null only if the statute is silent on education.

How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

example.quote: A person may not submit a bid or work as a contractor until that person has been issued a certificate of registration as a contractor by the department.

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)
e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'
Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: Required for residential contractor endorsement; offered at least once each year in each judicial district; may be written or practical.

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.
Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.
Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

The department shall require at least eight hours of continuing competency activity for each licensing period.

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']
Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: A board established under this title and the department, with respect to an occupation that it regulates under this title, may by regulation establish criteria for issuing a temporary courtesy license

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Temporary courtesy licenses may be issued to nonresidents by regulation; military courtesy licenses available to active duty members and spouses who hold a current license in another state with substantially equivalent requirements.

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development, unless the context indicates otherwise

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.
Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.

example.quote: each applicant shall, at the time of applying for a certificate of registration, file with the commissioner a surety bond running to the state

fields.meaning: Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.value: "contractor" means a person who, in the pursuit of an independent business, undertakes or offers to perform, or claims to have the capacity to perform, or submits a bid for a project to construct, alter, repair, move, or demolish a building, highway, road, railroad, or any type of fixed structure, including excavation and site development and erection of scaffolding; "contractor" includes a general contractor, builder, mechanical contractor, specialty contractor, and subcontractor

groups.intro: Fields discovered specifically for this profession (auto-derived from its statutes); they vary profession to profession.

fields.meaning: Whether the contractor's registration number must appear in all advertisements, contracts, estimates, and proposals.

example.quote: Advertising and contracts must also include the contractor's registration number.

fields.meaning: Minimum dollar amount of liability insurance covering personal injury that a contractor must maintain.

example.quote: $50,000 for injury, including death, to any one person, and $100,000 for injury, including death, to more than one person

fields.meaning: Minimum dollar amount of insurance covering property damage caused by the contractor's work.

example.quote: public liability and property damage insurance covering the applicant's contracting operations in this state in the sum of not less than $20,000 for damage to property

fields.meaning: Whether a contractor may satisfy insurance requirements by attesting to being self-insured rather than carrying a third-party policy.

example.quote: a valid workers' compensation self-insurance certificate issued by the Alaska Workers' Compensation Board

fields.meaning: Whether a home improvement contract must be in writing to be valid and enforceable against the owner.
Number of business days within which an owner may rescind a signed home improvement contract without penalty.
Maximum fraction of the total contract price a contractor may collect as a deposit before work begins, for contracts above a threshold amount.
Minimum contract price above which the deposit cap rule applies.
Whether any deviation from the original plans or specifications requires a written change order signed by both parties.
Whether a home improvement contract may include an arbitration clause, subject to specific formatting and disclosure requirements.
List of clause types that, if included in a home improvement contract, make the contract voidable by the owner.
Minimum total cash value of home improvements in the prior taxable year below which a person is exempt from contractor registration.
Minimum cash price of a single project for the work to qualify as a regulated home improvement requiring a registered contractor.
Whether the statute defines a specific criminal offense of home improvement fraud with enumerated prohibited acts.
Dollar amount above which a home improvement fraud violation is graded as a felony rather than a misdemeanor.
Whether the grading of a fraud offense is elevated by one level when the victim is 60 years of age or older.
Whether state registration preempts local governments from imposing their own contractor registration fees or licensing requirements.
Whether existing local licensing standards for specific trades (e.g., electricians, plumbers) are preserved notwithstanding state preemption.
How often, in years, a contractor must renew their registration with the issuing authority.

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: Whether a contractor must report to the state any disciplinary action taken against them in another jurisdiction.
